new_or_changed_cards.support_text: The impact of ester hydrolysis on cellular toxicity was evaluated using propidium iodide uptake, to measure necrotic changes. (Prior administration of the calcium chelator BAPTA had previously been shown to prevent this toxicity.)

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: experimental_system=Ex vivo human precision-cut liver slices (PCLS), Homo sapiens liver tissue; treated slices (CP + bile acids) compared to DMSO vehicle + bile acids. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Differentially expressed genes in slices exposed to the cholestatic drugs in the presence of bile acids versus slices exposed to vehicle (DMSO) in the presence of bile acids were identified using the unpaired moderated t test in the limma package. RNA was isolated from slices with <10, <30 and 30-50% decreased viability.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To test the link between SAM and PEMT in LRH-1 target gene expression, the authors treated cells with 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity, and with a high dose acute homocysteine treatment that disrupts SAM-to-SAH flow. Both DZA and acute homocysteine treatments decreased mRNA expression of Lrh-1 target genes including Cyp8b1 and Shp, and reduced LRH-1 Gal4-LBD luciferase reporter activity. Expression of several other LRH-1 target genes, including Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2 and Mdr3, was also reduced upon DZA or homocysteine treatment.

Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes expressing a kinase-dead LKB1 (dominant-negative) construct | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=200 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=24 h exposure, endpoint read at 24 h | exposure_regimen=single_continuous | extra_details=Molecule role: AMPK activator. AICAR alone increased canalicular length to 103% in rat hepatocytes (94% in human); viability 99% in both species. No effect of AICAR alone was an injury reduction; it maintained polarization. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Rat hepatocytes treated for 24h with 200μM AICAR alone retained 103% canalicular length, and 99% viability, relative to control.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes expressing a kinase-dead LKB1 (dominant-negative) construct | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: experimental_system=In vitro; human; PHHs and dHepaRG cells; monoculture; no immune cells; metabolic competence not stated. | analytical_platform_and_normalization=Gene-expression measurement; platform not specified in this window (quantitative RT-PCR implied).

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=up to 100 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=48-72 h exposure | exposure_regimen=single_continuous | extra_details=Focal molecule ATI-2173 (5'-phosphoramidate of clevudine). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: ATI-2173 was evaluated for potential acute cellular and mitochondrial toxicity. Nonproliferating cells (cryopreserved primary human hepatocytes, cryopreserved iCell cardiomyocytes, and cryopreserved human bone marrow mononuclear cells) were incubated with increasing concentrations of ATI-2173 or the control compound doxorubicin. ATI-2173 up to 100 μM did not demonstrate any cytotoxicity in primary hepatocytes, kidney cells, or cardiomyocytes.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Primary human hepatocytes (PHHs), cryopreserved human hepatocyte preparation
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=Cytotoxicity assessment—50% cytotoxic concentration (CC50); exact plate/kit method in Fig. S1
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Molecule label ATI-2173. CC50 measured in the same assay as the PHH anti-HBV EC50 (1.31 nM); CC50 >20 nM indicates no 50% viability loss through the top tested concentration. peg-IFN-alpha2a (EC50 2 IU/ml, CC50 >100 IU/ml) was an additional control in these PHH assays. Results shown in Fig. S1. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: ATI-2173 was incubated with HepG2.2.15 cells and primary human hepatocytes, and in the same anti-HBV assay a 50% cytotoxic concentration was measured: ATI-2173 showed an EC50 of 1.31 nM and a CC50 >20 nM in primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) (Fig. S1).

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In EGF-stimulated primary rat hepatocytes, the addition of ribavirin inhibited [3H]-thymidine uptake in a dose-dependent fashion. Exposure of EGF-treated rat hepatocytes for 3 days to 1 µmol/L and 50 µmol/L ribavirin resulted, respectively, in a significant decrease and a nearly complete suppression of DNA synthesis without appearance of morphological changes. [3H]-Thymidine incorporation was also effectively suppressed by mycophenolic acid at 10 µmol/L without any toxic effect.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To test the link between SAM and PEMT in LRH-1 target gene expression, the authors treated cells with 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity, and with a high dose acute homocysteine treatment that disrupts SAM-to-SAH flow. Expression of several other LRH-1 target genes, including Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2 and Mdr3, was also reduced upon DZA or homocysteine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=Cytotoxicity assessment in cryopreserved human hepatocytes—qualitative outcome
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. Cytotoxicity result is qualitative with no numeric potency, assay readout, exposure duration, or vehicle concentration reported in the provided text; the 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) top concentration and <10% CYP inhibition are reported for the enzyme-activity evaluation, which is a CYP assay without a concurrent hepatocyte health/reserve endpoint and is therefore not extracted as an eligible hepatocyte phenotype. No quantitative or regimen details for the cytotoxicity assessment were supplied in the text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. The same in-vitro study showed significant cell uptake by analysing cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium, and all evaluated CYP enzyme activities had <10% inhibition at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) of mipomersen sodium.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. This is source terminology; the canalicular phenotype alone does not validate a direct or selective AMPK target mechanism. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Reverse transcriptase inhibitors inhibited MRP1 in vitro using CMF as the probe. With the exception of abacavir (no effect on MRP3), all the tested compounds increased intracellular CMF fluorescence in a concentration-dependent manner in cell lines overexpressing MRP2 or MRP3; emtricitabine exhibited the most pronounced inhibitory effect together with delavirdine and efavirenz.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Leonurine treatment of NAFLD mice was evaluated by RNA sequencing of liver samples. RNA-seq, using FPKM as the expression metric, found 826 DEGs between the normal control (NC) and model (M) groups (458 up, 368 down), and 59 DEGs between the M and leonurine-treated (LH) groups, comprising 20 up-regulated and 39 down-regulated genes. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In a time- and concentration-dependent manner, HepG2 cells became highly sensitive towards death receptor-mediated cell death (induced by CD95L, TRAIL or TNF) when pre-treated with sub-toxic concentrations of 5-aza-CR. 5-aza-CR-enabled hepatocyte cell death was characterized by classical hallmarks of apoptosis such as membrane blebbing, chromatin condensation and exposure of phosphatidyl serine on the outer membrane. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: experimental_system=In vivo mouse (Mus musculus) model of bile-acid-induced hepatic ER stress; liver-specific XBP1 knockout (LS-XBP1-/-) and XBP1fl/fl (floxed) control mice, both adult and weanling ages; hepatocyte ER stress / UPR response; serum and liver protein readouts.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_family=protein_signaling_or_enzyme_activity | endpoint_and_comparator=Hepatic CHOP (DNA damage-inducible transcript 3 protein) expression as a molecular signature of unresolved ER stress after CA exposure, compared between liver-specific XBP1 deletion (LS-XBP1-/-) and XBP1fl/fl controls in adult vs weanling mice; the finding is that deleting hepatic XBP1 in adult mice, but not weanling mice, increased CHOP expression, i.e., loss of XBP1 sensitized adult mice to CA-induced ER stress.
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_schedule=CA (cholic acid, CpA) administered in the diet to adult (and weanling) LS-XBP1-/- and XBP1fl/fl mice; CA feeding in the cholestatic bile-acid / ER-stress model; specific feeding duration and CA dose not stated in this window. | extra_details=Adult LS-XBP1-/- mice fed CA showed elevated serum ALT comparable to weanling WT and XBP1fl/fl mice; loss of hepatic XBP1 did not produce further injury in weanlings (no additional CHOP increase in weanlings), whereas it increased CHOP in adults. This is a molecular (protein) ER-stress signature explicitly linked to hepatic cholestatic injury susceptibility; the CA dose, feeding duration, and western-blot method are outside the provided text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We fed CA to LS-XBP1-/- and XBP1fl/fl mice. Adult LS-XBP1-/- mice fed CA had increased serum ALT levels similar to both WT and XBP1fl/fl weanling mice, while loss of hepatic XBP1 did not produce further injury in the weanlings. Liver-specific deletion of XBP1 in adult mice, but not weanling mice, led to increased CHOP protein expression, supporting that deleting hepatic XBP1 sensitized adult mice to CA-induced ER stress and hepatocyte injury.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: experimental_system=Ex vivo human precision-cut liver slices (PCLS), Homo sapiens liver tissue; treated slices (CP + bile acids) compared to DMSO vehicle + bile acids. new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: immune_stimulus_regimen=bile acids present in the exposure medium (cholestatic co-condition), dose not stated | exposure_schedule=Human PCLS exposed to CP in the presence of bile acids for the transcriptomic assay; comparator was vehicle (DMSO) in the presence of bile acids; RNA sampled from slices with <10 %, <30 % and 30-50 % decreased viability. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Differentially expressed genes in slices exposed to the cholestatic drugs in the presence of bile acids versus slices exposed to vehicle (DMSO) in the presence of bile acids were identified using the unpaired moderated t test in the limma package. RNA was isolated from slices with <10, <30 and 30-50% decreased viability.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_role=parent | mechanistic_entities_and_components=focal substrate: C-11 palmitate (CPA); oxidation product: C-11 CO2; esterified intracellular lipid pool: C-11 lipid; modifiers of MVO2: pacing, methoxamine, local xylazine applied to sinus node; modifier of MBF: dipyridamole | exposure_time=45 minutes of C-11 time-activity recording; early rapid phase and late slow phase halftime analyses | extra_details=32 experiments on 19 dogs; MVO2 altered by pacing, intravenous methoxamine, or local xylazine application; MBF increased by dipyridamole; CPT/FAO-enzyme activity not directly assayed, FAO flux measured through radiolabeled CO2 production in vivo. Extraction fraction and clearance rates were determined from the peak and slope of the myocardial C-11 time-activity curve. Extraction fraction was independent of flow, oxygen consumption, arterial FFA and glucose, pH, and myocardial FFA/glucose consumption. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Following C-11 palmitate (CPA) injection into the left circumflex coronary artery of dogs, myocardial C-11 time-activity curves were recorded for 45 minutes. CPA oxidation was assessed via C-11 CO2 production; the early rapid-phase halftime (3.39 ± 0.70 min in controls) was a function of myocardial oxygen consumption (r = 0.84) and C-11 CO2 production (r = 0.97), and the ratio of C-11 CO2 production to C-11 lipid washout averaged 4.2:1 in controls, increasing with cardiac work. CPA extraction fraction averaged 0.65 ± 0.10 in controls and was independent of flow, oxygen consumption, arterial FFA and glucose, and myocardial FFA/glucose consumption. The late slow phase (halftime 166.55 ± 46.53 min) was associated with a C-11 CO2 to C-11 lipid washout ratio of 3.0:1 and was attributed to turnover of intracellular esterified CPA.

new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: reported_result=CPA extraction fraction averaged 0.65 ± 0.10 in controls; early rapid-phase halftime 3.39 ± 0.70 min correlated with C-11 CO2 production (r = 0.97) and with MVO2 (r = 0.84); ratio of C-11 CO2 production to C-11 lipid washout averaged 4.2:1 in controls; late-phase halftime 166.55 ± 46.53 min with C-11 CO2:C-11 lipid washout ratio 3.0:1
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_role=parent | mechanistic_entities_and_components=focal substrate: C-11 palmitate (CPA); oxidation product: C-11 CO2; esterified intracellular lipid pool: C-11 lipid; modifiers of MVO2: pacing, methoxamine, local xylazine applied to sinus node; modifier of MBF: dipyridamole | exposure_time=45 minutes of C-11 time-activity recording; early rapid phase and late slow phase halftime analyses | extra_details=32 experiments on 19 dogs; MVO2 altered by pacing, intravenous methoxamine, or local xylazine application; MBF increased by dipyridamole; CPT/FAO-enzyme activity not directly assayed, FAO flux measured through radiolabeled CO2 production in vivo. Extraction fraction and clearance rates were determined from the peak and slope of the myocardial C-11 time-activity curve. Extraction fraction was independent of flow, oxygen consumption, arterial FFA and glucose, pH, and myocardial FFA/glucose consumption. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Following C-11 palmitate (CPA) injection into the left circumflex coronary artery of dogs, myocardial C-11 time-activity curves were recorded for 45 minutes. CPA oxidation was assessed via C-11 CO2 production; the early rapid-phase halftime (3.39 ± 0.70 min in controls) was a function of myocardial oxygen consumption (r = 0.84) and C-11 CO2 production (r = 0.97), and the ratio of C-11 CO2 production to C-11 lipid washout averaged 4.2:1 in controls, increasing with cardiac work. CPA extraction fraction averaged 0.65 ± 0.10 in controls and was independent of flow, oxygen consumption, arterial FFA and glucose, and myocardial FFA/glucose consumption. The late slow phase (halftime 166.55 ± 46.53 min) was associated with a C-11 CO2 to C-11 lipid washout ratio of 3.0:1 and was attributed to turnover of intracellular esterified CPA.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Following C-11 palmitate (CPA) injection into the left circumflex coronary artery of dogs, myocardial C-11 time-activity curves were recorded for 45 minutes. CPA oxidation was assessed via C-11 CO2 production; the early rapid-phase halftime (3.39 ± 0.70 min in controls) was a function of myocardial oxygen consumption (r = 0.84) and C-11 CO2 production (r = 0.97), and the ratio of C-11 CO2 production to C-11 lipid washout averaged 4.2:1 in controls, increasing with cardiac work. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Following C-11 palmitate (CPA) injection into the left circumflex coronary artery of dogs, myocardial C-11 time-activity curves were recorded for 45 minutes. CPA oxidation was assessed via C-11 CO2 production; the early rapid-phase halftime (3.39 ± 0.70 min in controls) was a function of myocardial oxygen consumption (r = 0.84) and C-11 CO2 production (r = 0.97), and the ratio of C-11 CO2 production to C-11 lipid washout averaged 4.2:1 in controls, increasing with cardiac work. The late slow phase (halftime 166.55 ± 46.53 min) was associated with a C-11 CO2 to C-11 lipid washout ratio of 3.0:1 and was attributed to turnover of intracellular esterified CPA.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=cultured cortical astrocytic cells; in vitro OGD ischemia model | assay_and_platform=DCF fluorescence emission assay; fluorescence (fold increase from control)
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (DCF fluorescence)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (DCF fluorescence)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes expressing a kinase-dead LKB1 (dominant-negative) construct | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. This is source terminology; the canalicular phenotype alone does not validate a direct or selective AMPK target mechanism. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Treatment with two different AC inhibitors, 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine and MDL-12330A, completely blocked taurocholate-stimulated canalicular network formation in primary rat hepatocytes [116].

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.
